key_insight: Small language models can be aligned more reliably with PPO when the base model is fluent and the reward signal is strong, but only if several low-level training failures are explicitly prevented.
engineering_relevance: The paper provides practical fixes for unstable RLHF-style training in 70M–500M parameter agents, making small-scale language model alignment more reproducible and safer to deploy.
method: Diagnosed three failure modes: LoRA freezing, bf16 importance-ratio overflow, and reward-model-driven collapse.
Applied merge-and-reinitialize adapters, float32 PPO updates, and a safety stack with reward whitening, ratio guarding, and weight rollback.
Tested 15 model–corpus setups across Pythia and SmolLM2 on TinyStories, CNN/DailyMail, and Wikitext-103.
evidence_signal: Across the evaluated configurations, the stabilized PPO pipeline converged consistently and improved preference win rate over SFT baselines when the prior model was fluent and the reward was informative.
watch_item: The approach still depends on a sufficiently strong supervised starting point and reliable reward modeling, so weaker priors or noisy rewards may limit gains.
paper_title: Towards Robust Reinforcement Learning for Small-Scale Language Model Agents
